findings.trigger: A recurring task (say a daily restart) is due; execute_task writes last_run_ts (>= next_run_ts) before it acts (comment at :441-445), then a DDC exception such as DockerConnectionError escapes it (comment at :536-542 says every DDC exception does). execute_single_task (:563) only logs the error; next_run_ts is not advanced and nothing undoes last_run_ts. On every following cycle the guard at :446 sees last_run_ts >= next_run_ts and `continue`s with an INFO line 'was already begun ...; not repeating it' - BEFORE the missed-run handling at :466 that would move the task to its next occurrence. The task never fires again and is never rescheduled; the web panel still shows it as active with a next_run in the past. The C6 fix (do not mark the run as executed before it happened) is undone by this guard for exactly the case it was made for.
findings.suggestion: Make the 'already begun' guard apply only to occurrences begun by ANOTHER process (e.g. only when last_run_ts was written before this service started, or within a short window), or on an escaped exception in execute_single_task advance/reschedule the task (or reset last_run_ts) so the missed-run path at :466 can reach it. Log the permanent skip at WARNING rather than INFO in any case.
findings.unsure_why: execute_task is outside this section; I rely on the two comments in this file that say it writes last_run_ts before acting and that DDC exceptions escape it without advancing next_run_ts. If execute_task resets last_run_ts or advances next_run_ts on its failure paths, the trap does not exist.

findings.trigger: The warning is only posted when a check cycle happens to land inside [acting_at - warn*60, acting_at). The cycle period is CHECK_INTERVAL plus the cycle's own execution time, and grows to 120 s (execution > 5 s), 180 s (concurrency cap) or up to 300 s (error path; DDC_SCHEDULER_CHECK_INTERVAL is operator-configurable). A panel task with warn_minutes=1 (normalize_options allows 1-60) at the default 60 s interval has a window shorter than one period, so consecutive checks can straddle it; with a configured interval of 600 s even the Discord options 5/10 min are straddled. When that happens the check at or after acting_at sees the occurrence as due, `_players_allow` says yes, and the restart/stop runs WITHOUT the warning the operator configured - no log line says the warning was skipped, `_warned` is simply never set.
findings.suggestion: When an occurrence is about to be queued (after :476) and warn_minutes > 0 but self._warned.get(task_id) != next_run_ts, either post the warning right then ('restarts in 1 minute' / 'now') or at least log at WARNING that the warning window was missed. Alternatively refuse warn_minutes*60 < CHECK_INTERVAL in normalize_options, or clamp the sleep so that a pending warning window is never slept through.

findings.trigger: Hosted mode: stop() followed by start() before the loop has processed the cancellation (e.g. a restart path or a test that stops and restarts the global service). stop() sets running=False and schedules the cancel of task T1; start() sets running=True and creates T2. When T1's CancelledError arrives, the `finally` in _service_loop_supervised (:208-210) sets self.running=False, self.event_loop=None and self._service_task=None - the flags that now belong to T2. T2 leaves its `while self.running` loop after its first cycle, start() has already returned True, and no scheduled task runs any more; get_service_stats reports running=False, the log only shows 'hosted-task ended'. Standalone mode has the mirror problem: stop() joins the thread for 2 s while the old loop sleeps up to 60-300 s; a following start() sets running=True again, the old loop never exits, and two scheduler loops run side by side (and when one eventually ends, its `finally` at :271-274 clears event_loop/running for the other).
findings.suggestion: Make the finally blocks conditional on identity: only clear self.running/_service_task/event_loop if self._service_task is still this task (or the thread is still self.thread); or generate a per-run token in start() and have the loop check `self._run_token == mine` instead of the shared `self.running`. In start(), refuse or wait while a previous task/thread is still alive.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see whether any code path in production calls stop() then start() on the same instance; if only process shutdown calls stop(), the trap is never hit outside tests.

findings.trigger: A task with wait_for_empty is due while players are online. At that moment the status cache entry for the container has data.success False (Docker query hiccup) or players_online None (game query timed out / server under load) -> players_online() returns None -> occupied() treats it as 0 -> should_act() returns True and the restart/stop runs at once while people are playing. warning_due() with wait_for_empty also returns False on such counts, so no warning goes out either. Nothing is logged: the INFO 'waits: N player(s) online' line is only written when the gate holds. The module docstring says 'unreadable counts as EMPTY' was decided and that the save-time check (query_problem) makes this 'never a surprise' - but query_problem only sees the state at save time; a count that is readable then and fails at 04:00 is exactly a surprise.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish 'container not running' (0) from 'unknown' (None) at run time: while waiting, treat None as 'still occupied' until acting_at (the daily restart is still guaranteed by the max wait) and log at WARNING when a count could not be read; or, if the operator wants 'unknown = empty' also at run time, log that decision at WARNING each time it lets an action through.
findings.unsure_why: The module docstring records 'unknown counts as empty' as an operator decision. I cannot tell whether that decision was meant to cover transient failures at run time, or only containers whose count cannot be read at all (which is what the save-time check covers).

findings.trigger: A wait_for_empty task or rule is saved for a GROUP whose members cannot be resolved (group service raises, or the group has no members). target_containers() returns [] (WARNING in the log only), query_problems() iterates nothing and returns [] -> the operator sees 'Saved: only when nobody plays' with no notice, although at run time counts_for([]) is {} and occupied({}) is False, so the action runs at the scheduled time regardless of players. The docstring promise 'the operator is told there if not' does not hold for this case.
findings.suggestion: In query_problems, report a problem when is_group is True and target_containers() returned no containers ('group could not be resolved / has no members - the player check is skipped'), so the same notice reaches the operator as for a single container.
findings.unsure_why: Depends on whether group_service.members_of() can return an empty or missing group at save time; the group may be validated earlier on the creation path I cannot see.

findings.trigger: normalize_options receives wait_for_empty as a non-empty string, e.g. {'wait_for_empty': 'false', 'warn_minutes': 0} from a form or query string -> bool('false') is True -> the task is saved with wait_for_empty=True and max_wait_minutes=120; a restart the user switched the wait OFF for now waits up to two hours for an empty server. The two whole-minute fields are parsed with int() and refused on garbage, this one is not.
findings.suggestion: Parse the flag like the numbers: accept bool, 0/1, and the strings 'true'/'false'/'on'/'off' explicitly, refuse anything else with a reason.
findings.unsure_why: The web panel and the rules editor are outside this section; if every caller sends a JSON boolean (the Discord path does), the trigger never occurs.

notes: Two places compute the same warning window: player_gate.warning_due (:133-134) and SchedulerService._warn_players_if_due (:358-359); identical today, will drift if one changes. _warned is set (:363) BEFORE post_warning runs, so a warning that reached 0 channels (bot None, channels not cached) is never retried for that occurrence - logged at WARNING, so acceptable, but worth knowing. The scheduler warning text uses task.container_name (docker name / group name), not the display name the players know. A warning is posted even if execute_task later refuses the action (B14 unreadable config, disallowed action) - a 'restarts in 10 minutes' that does not happen; rare. _warned/_waiting grow with task ids and are never pruned - negligible. In _check_and_execute_tasks a non-dict task.options (hand-edited tasks.json) would raise AttributeError at :355 and the outer except at :514 aborts the whole cycle for ALL tasks - the loop's general per-task-exception weakness, not new to this section. hold_until_empty holds the calling coroutine for up to 720 min; whether the auto-action caller tolerates that I cannot see. _may_edit passes the group name to _admin_may_control for a group task; whether a container-scoped admin (B2 refinement) is refused there but allowed on the creation path I cannot see. In standalone mode _run_service sets the uvloop policy globally after creating the loop with the default policy - harmless but ineffective. warning_text says 'will restart' for RECREATE auto-actions (gated_verb maps it to restart) - acceptable wording.
